items.fromString:
On the Fedora side there's an ongoing problem that we get *a lot* of tickets on Bugzilla for CVEs filed against packages that are either
 * not affected by the issue,
 * already updated to a version that doesn't have the issue, or
 * the *wrong* package entirely, usually due to some name confusion or similarity.

Anecdotally, the CVE reports that I have been "involved" with recently had false positive rates between ~65% and 95%. At the point where the _majority_ of filed tickets is wrong they're just noise and I do not blame package maintainers that they're getting tired of them.

One thing that appears to be a common source of "mistakes" or "mis-filings" seems to be poor quality of the data used to associate upstream project names with package names in Fedora (for example, bugs for a CVE in an NPM / JavaScript package called "elliptic" are filed against packages for a Rust library named "elliptic-curve").

We have been wondering if it would help this process (and possibly other things too, SBOM something something) to add more reliable - and standardized metadata to packages.

I suggested using the PURL format: [https://github.com/package-url/purl-spec]

It looks like this standard is also used / supported by SBOM formats like CycloneDX and SPDX, so having package metadata like this could also be useful for other purposes.

If this sounds like a desirable thing to do or have, then we would draft an addition to the Fedora Packaging Guidelines to document how to add PURL metadata to packages, and / or integrate generating this metadata into existing RPM Provides generators.

(No idea what the 1029830 further input fields below "Desciption" are for in this form, so I'm going to ignore them.)

items.fromString:
Every week members of Fedora, RHEL, and CentOS Leadership ("FRCL") meet to discuss topics of shared interest.  Rather than finished presentations we discuss works in progress  that create opportunities for collaboration and minimize opportunities for unwelcome surprises.  The meeting is recorded, published, and leads are encouraged to take the results back to their respective communities for further consideration.

Invites: All FRCL members are invited and all community members are welcome. Contact Brendan for an invite if you would like one.

Chat: Between meetings people chat in #FRCL on Matrix.

Invites: All FRCL members are invited and all community members are welcome. Contact [~accountid:557058:830d7ab4-c24b-4ec7-b2f5-ed1d9e873189] for an invite if you would like one.
